title: P300 dataset BI2015a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 43 healthy subjects performing a visual P300-based brain-computer interface task using the Brain Invaders videogame paradigm. Participants responded to an oddball stimulus presentation (36-symbol grid with 1 target, 35 non-targets) across three sessions with varying flash durations (110ms, 80ms, 50ms). EEG data were acquired using 32 wet electrodes at 512 Hz and processed with a calibration-free adaptive Riemannian classifier for real-time feedback. Resting state recordings (eyes closed) were acquired before and after sessions.
methods_description: EEG recordings were acquired using 32 active wet electrodes (g.GAMMAcap, g.tec) at 512 Hz sampling rate with right earlobe reference and Fz ground. The oddball paradigm presented pseudo-randomly flashed symbol groups on a 36-symbol grid. Three game sessions (9 levels each) employed different flash durations (110ms, 80ms, 50ms). Real-time classification used an adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean (RMDM) classifier. Resting state recordings (eyes closed) were acquired before and after sessions. Data were collected using OpenViBE software with synchronized USB tagging to minimize jitter.
